summary.text: TPC / TPEE is a thermoplastic copolyester elastomer. Makers sell it for parts that bend continuously and for soft parts in fashion and healthcare, and its glass transition is -35 °C. On the H2C most products print at 220 °C without chamber heat. Makers warn that it needs a direct-drive extruder and a low print speed, and that it can shed a little powder.

notApplicable.hdt045: HDT is a rigid-bar test. ISO 75 ends at 0.2 % outer-fibre strain, which a bar reaches once its modulus falls to about 225 MPa, so an elastomer has no meaningful HDT and makers list it as N/A. A value an elastomer's sheet publishes is shown and never decides. Sintering filaments are left out too: the finished part is the sintered metal or ceramic.

items.text: Arnitel® ID flexible 3D printing grade based on >50% renewable content.

Warping: Corners of the print lift and detach from the platform. Advice is to increase the build plate temperature. Wait long enough to allow the heat to dissipate to the top surface of the substrate.
In order to prevent moisture pick up and contamination, supplied packaging should be kept closed and undamaged.
For the same reason, partially used bags should be sealed before re-storage.
Allow the material that has been stored elsewhere to adapt to the temperature in the processing room while keeping the bag closed.
Arnitel® ID grades are supplied in airtight, moisture-proof packaging.
Arnitel® ID grades are packaged at a moisture level <0.1 w%.
To prevent moisture condensing on filaments, bring cold filaments up to ambient temperature in the print shop while keeping the packaging close.
Note that for different nozzle diameters the settings should be changed accordingly.
Due to its flexible nature direct drive extruders will be recommended.
Common fused filament fabrication (FFF) equipment should work with Arnitel® filaments.
However, Bowden type extruders modified for use with flexible filaments are known to work as well.
To generate a homogeneous melt, the melt temperature should always be above 200°C / 392°F.
Optimal mechanical properties will be achieved at melt temperature in the given range.
Prior to removing the printed part from the bed, the bed temperature should be lowered to ambient to avoid severe deformation of the part.
For the best adhesion with Arnitel® ID it is advised to use an adhesive promotor, e.g. glue-stick or 3D-Lac®.
Alternatively, printing on bare glass can be used at elevated temperatures when using a large footprint, e.g. by using a large brim.
Prior to applying an adhesive promotor or to printing on bare substrate, the surface must be free of dirt and grease.
Therefore cleaning with ethanol or acetone is recommended.
It is advised to add a brim of at least 5 mm to the print.
Production has to be started with a clean machine.
Starting the machine, extrude at least 50 mm of new filament through the nozzle.
Remove the filament from the machine before shutting down your printer.
During production breaks longer than a few minutes, purge the nozzle adequately.

First layer not sticking / parts coming loose: The first layer of your print does not seem to want to stick or your parts come loose partway through the print. Remedies: check bed levelling and first layer thickness, increase size of brim, raise bed temperature, add appropriate adhesion promotor e.g. 3D-Lac® or glue-stick the build plate or change to PEI bed substrate.

Filament grinding: The feeder wheels have ground a groove into the filament. Remove the damaged filament and start again, reduce printing speed, disable retraction or reduce retraction speed and length
Stringing: Unwanted strands of plastic span across the print. Lower nozzle temperature, increase travel speed of the print head.

items.text: The TPC is used in dynamic applications where prolonged constant flexibility is required, such as applications where material is continuously bent becomes.

TPC also has high strength making it resistant to damage.

Only printable with Direct Drive Extruder - low printing speed

items.text: FiberFlex 30D is a flexible TPU filament with a Shore hardness of 30D , designed for users who need a very soft , rubber-like material for 3D printing.

Thanks to its exceptional flexibility, it is perfect for creating prints that are resistant to bending , crushing , and stretching , making it an excellent choice for applications requiring high mechanical strength and flexibility .
FiberFlex 30D is designed for more advanced users who want to use flexible TPU materials for complex projects.
A Shore hardness of 30D provides noticeable flexibility and a soft-to-the-touch surface.
High impact resistance is maintained even at low temperatures, so the print won't crack when struck in cold weather.
The material retains its shape and strength even when exposed to heat.
Its chemical resistance makes the material suitable for use in industrial environments.

However, printing with FiberFlex 30D filament requires some experience and a printer equipped with a direct-drive extruder, due to the material’s softness, which can pose challenges during filament feeding.
NOTE: FiberFlex 30D may release a small amount of powder during printing; this is a natural characteristic of the material and does not constitute a product defect.
Drying conditions: 60°C / 4 hours
It is recommended to lower the print speed and reduce the extruder pressure to ensure a stable, high-quality print.

If you notice a significant amount of powder buildup, we recommend periodically cleaning the printer components, as this buildup can, over time, interfere with the proper feeding of filament into the extruder.
Heating is not required but recommended

products.composition: "1,3-Benzenedicarboxylic acid, dimethyl ester, polymer with 1,4-butanediol, dimethyl 1,4- benzenedicarboxylate and 9086-55-9 - >81" (D-FIBERLOGY-MATTFLEX-40D-SDS-EN, p. 2)

items.text: Compatible with BambuLab AMS.
This makes it user-friendly and suitable for both hobbyists and professional FDM users.

Thanks to its unique combination of flexibility and a matte finish, Fiberlogy MattFlex 40D is ideal for producing functional gaskets, shock absorbers, flexible hinges, protective covers, and load-bearing components.
At the same time, it’s ideal for projects where an elegant 3D print appearance is just as important as durability.
Fiberlogy MattFlex 40D is a filament for users who want to combine the advantages of flexible materials with an attractive, matte finish.
It is an excellent choice for both home and professional applications.
It is an excellent alternative to traditional TPU filaments, offering not only ease of printing but also a unique appearance for your prints.
The filament offers impressive strength: it can be stretched up to 6 times its original length, has a compression resistance of up to 50%, and exhibits high impact strength and elasticity.
Additionally, MattFlex 40D is resistant to chemicals and low temperatures, making it suitable for demanding technical and industrial applications.
Fiberlogy MattFlex 40D is a modern, flexible 3D printing filament that stands out for its matte finish and rubber-like properties.
The matte surface effectively hides layer lines, giving models an aesthetically pleasing look and eliminating the need for additional post-processing.
Drying conditions: 50°C / 4 hours
Unlike many flexible filaments, MattFlex 40D allows for high print speeds—up to 60 mm/s—without compromising quality.
Build surface: Smooth PEI + masking tape or adhesive; Textured PEI + adhesive; Glass + masking tape or adhesive
Enclosed chamber: not required
